Facts already established:
- Archer static eval is material 505 plus a piece-square table. No shot-target term.
- Ogre static eval is material 318 and a zero piece-square table. No shove-target term.
- Beast has a small adjacent-enemy bonus (10cp, cap 18) and no chain-length term. Leave it.
- A 24-game depth-2 sketch still saw ~3.42 shots and ~1.50 shoves per game (docs/research/shipped-balance-2026-09-24.md).

Read src/ai/search.ts enough to say, in one plain paragraph, whether a capture, a shot, and a shove are generated as moves the search can pick (so the material change is seen on the next position). Do not edit that file; another agent may be editing it. If you cannot tell, say so.

The conclusion to write, unless the code contradicts it: do not add a shot or shove bonus. The search already plays them because the result of the move changes material. A bonus would be a new value with no measurement.

Return: the one-paragraph finding and the doc path.
last_assistant_text:
**Finding:** In `src/ai/search.ts`, the main search builds legal moves with `genLegal(..., 'all')` via `genPiece`, then `apply`s each before scoring the child. Ordinary captures and archer shots both put victims in `captures` (shots use `to === from`); `apply` clears those squares, so the material change is already on the next position. Ogre shoves are separate moves (`captures: []` plus `shove`); `apply` relocates the piece (and under `push` moves the ogre onto the vacated square) but removes nothing, so material does not change—yet the search can still pick them. Quiescence only generates `captures`, so shots are in Q-search and shoves are not. Do not add a shot or shove bonus: shots are already driven by material, shoves already show up without a shove-target term, and either bonus would be a new unmeasured value.

task:
The user is in Cursor Desktop and keeps getting approval cards that say Allow when the agent runs commands, edits, or launches subagents. They want to approve in advance instead of pressing Allow each time.

Read current Cursor product documentation and answer with the exact settings path and control names as they exist now (2026). Cover:
1. Auto-run / YOLO / sandbox modes in Cursor Settings (Agents), including the chat composer control if there is one.
2. Command allowlist: how to add a command so it stops asking, including any "always allow" action on the card itself.
3. Whether Auto-review / smart-mode approval cards can be turned off or pre-approved, and what still always asks (network outside sandbox, git write, etc.).
4. The safest setting that stops the repeated Allow clicks for ordinary local tests (vitest, file edits) without turning off every safety check.

Return the steps in plain language a non-engineer can follow. Do not invent menu names. If a control moved, say where it is now. Cite the doc page titles.
last_assistant_text:
Here’s what the **current** Cursor docs say (2026). Older names like YOLO / Ask Every Time / Auto-Run still show up in older pages and forums; the live setting is named below.

---

## 1. Auto-run / YOLO / sandbox — where it lives now

**Path:** **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**  
(Also written as **Settings → Cursor Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**.)

Sources: [Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Terminal integration](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/terminal), [Auto-review Run Mode](https://cursor.com/changelog/auto-review).

**Run Mode** choices (Cursor 3.6+):

| Mode | What it does |
|------|----------------|
| **Auto-review** | Recommended default. Allowlisted calls run right away. Other shell commands run in the **sandbox** when they can. Anything else is checked by the Auto-review classifier. |
| **Allowlist** | Only allowlisted actions skip approval. Sandboxing for shell is optional (“Allowlist with sandboxing”). |
| **Run Everything** | Every tool call runs with no prompts. No sandbox. |

**Name changes (don’t look for these anymore as primary modes):**

- **Ask Every Time** — deprecated in 3.5; for the same behavior use **Allowlist** with an empty allowlist.
- **Run in Sandbox** — folded into **Allowlist** with sandboxing on.
- **YOLO** — not a current documented mode name; the “approve everything” option is **Run Everything**.

**Chat composer control:** Official docs only point to **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**. They do **not** document a separate Run Mode picker in the chat composer. Approval happens on the **approval card** in chat when something still needs you.

**Sandbox network modes** (same Run Modes page): **sandbox.json Only**, **sandbox.json + Defaults** (default), **Allow All**.

---

## 2. Command allowlist — stop asking for the same command

**In Settings**

1. Open **Settings → Agents → Approvals & Execution**.
2. Use the terminal / **Command allowlist** (entries like `npm`, `git status`, `vitest`).
3. Or put the same list in `~/.cursor/permissions.json` / project `.cursor/permissions.json` as `terminalAllowlist`.

Source: [permissions.json reference](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/permissions).

**On the approval card**

Docs name the action **Add to allowlist**. When `permissions.json` owns that allowlist, the in-app editor is read-only and **Add to allowlist** is hidden.

In the product/UI, people also see **Always Run** (e.g. Always Run `'git'`) for the same idea—add that command so it stops prompting. Prefer specific entries (`vitest`, `npm test`) over a bare `git` if you can.

**MCP:** Same place conceptually — `mcpAllowlist` or the in-app MCP allowlist; format `server:tool` (e.g. `github:*`).

---

## 3. Can Auto-review / “smart” approval cards be turned off or pre-approved?

**You choose the mode; you don’t fully “pre-approve Auto-review.”**

- Stay on **Auto-review** → fewer prompts, but the classifier can still block, and if the agent insists you still get an **approval prompt**. Docs say Auto-review is **best-effort**, not a hard security wall ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Governing agent autonomy with Auto-review](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-autonomy-auto-review)).
- Switch to **Allowlist** → no classifier; only allowlist (+ optional sandbox) decides.
- Switch to **Run Everything** → no approval cards for tool calls (highest risk).
- Steer Auto-review with plain English in `permissions.json` → `autoRun.allow_instructions` / `autoRun.block_instructions` (steering only, not a guarantee).

**What still asks even when a mode would otherwise auto-run** ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Agent Security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security)):

| Still needs you | Why |
|-----------------|-----|
| Commands that **can’t use the sandbox** | e.g. writes outside the workspace, privileged ops — Cursor shows they’re outside the sandbox and asks. |
| **Network** beyond sandbox policy | Sandbox network is limited unless you open it (defaults / `sandbox.json` / Allow All). |
| **Browser Protection** | Browser tools don’t auto-run. |
| **File-Deletion Protection** | Deletes (including `rm`) still need approval. |
| **External-File Protection** | Create/modify/delete **outside** the workspace still needs approval. |
| **Configuration files** | Workspace code edits usually auto-apply; config/settings-style files need approval. |
| **MCP** | After connecting a server, each tool call still needs approval unless it’s on the MCP allowlist. |
| Classifier block → agent retries with you | Auto-review can still surface a normal approval card. |

**Ordinary workspace file edits and reading/searching** do **not** need Allow by default ([Agent Security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security)).

**Subagents:** [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents) does not describe a separate “Allow subagent” toggle. Shell/MCP/Fetch they run still follow the same Run Mode / approvals.

---

## 4. Safest setup that cuts Allow clicks for normal local tests (vitest, edits)

Plain steps:

1. Open **Cursor Settings**.
2. Go to **Agents → Approvals & Execution**.
3. Set **Run Mode** to **Auto-review** (not **Run Everything**).
4. Leave sandbox network on **sandbox.json + Defaults** unless you need more.
5. Keep **Browser Protection**, **File-Deletion Protection**, and **External-File Protection** on.
6. When vitest/`npm test`/`pnpm` still prompts once, use **Add to allowlist** / **Always Run** for that command — or add `vitest`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `node` under the Command allowlist in the same settings page.
7. Optional: ask the agent to add soft guidance in `permissions.json`, e.g. allow tests/linters, block AWS/git push — only works in **Auto-review**.

That is the setup Cursor itself recommends as the “safest useful” default: **Auto-review** + sandbox + allowlist for repeat safe commands, without turning every guard off ([Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes), [Security and Privacy Hardening](https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/security-hardening)).

**Avoid for day-to-day coding:** **Run Everything** — zero prompts, no sandbox.

---

### Quick “where did it go?”

| Old / informal name | Now |
|---------------------|-----|
| YOLO / auto-run everything | **Run Everything** |
| Ask every time | Empty **Allowlist** |
| Run in Sandbox | **Allowlist** + sandboxing |
| Settings → Agents → Auto-Run (older Browser docs) | Prefer **Approvals & Execution** for Run Mode; Browser page may still say **Agents → Auto-Run** for browser allow/block lists |

Doc titles cited: **Run Modes**, **Agent Security**, **permissions.json reference**, **Terminal integration**, **Auto-review Run Mode**, **Browser**, **Governing agent autonomy with Auto-review**, **Security and Privacy Hardening**.

|--------|--------|

| Repetition | `Draw — threefold repetition` |
| Insufficient material | `Draw — insufficient material` |

Repo: /Users/za/Documents/king down chess. King+pawn vs king+paladin is playing, not a material draw. Depth 1 plays Ka1-b2 and scores -298. A pawn is worth 100 and a paladin is worth 408, so from White's side 100-408=-308. The gap from -308 to -298 is 10. Do not retune values. Do not change search. Do not edit src/ai/pawn-paladin-search.test.ts or any existing test. Do not commit. Paladin is not in the random pool. The negative score is not a bug to fix.

You own NEW file src/ai/pawn-paladin-why.test.ts. White king a1, white pawn a2, black king a8, black paladin d8, white to move. Break the static eval before the move and after Ka1-b2 into pawn value, paladin value, pawn square, paladin square, and king safety. Lock the numbers. Say whether -298 is the position after the king step.

Run: npx vitest run src/ai/pawn-paladin-why.test.ts

Return: the static before the move, the score after Ka1-b2, and the terms that make up the gap from -308.
last_assistant_text:
**Static before:** −321  
**After Ka1-b2:** −298 — yes, that is White’s static view of the position after the king step.

**Gap from −308 to −298 (+10):**
| term | White POV |
|---|---|
| pawn square (a2) | +20 |
| paladin square (d8) | −14 |
| paladin reach (20 × 1) | −20 |
| king safety (Kb2) | +24 |

`20 − 14 − 20 + 24 = +10`. Reach is unchanged by the step; only king safety moves (Ka1 ≈ +1 → Kb2 +24), which is why −321 becomes −298.

New file: `src/ai/pawn-paladin-why.test.ts` — vitest 1/1 pass.

On FEN 4r2k/8/8/8/2n3n1/2n3n1/8/M1P1K3, Ma1<>e1 then Re8xe1 leaves White not in check and with no legal move: stalemate. That is locked in src/rules/swap-escape-block.test.ts. Depth-2 search of the starting FEN scores the swap -1689 (src/ai/maester-safe-escape.test.ts).

negamax returns 0 for no moves when depth is still positive. When depth hits 0 it calls quiesce first. Quiesce stand-pat uses evalBoard and only treats no-moves as mate when in check. A stalemate exactly at the horizon can be scored as lost material.

You own NEW file src/ai/stalemate-horizon.test.ts. From the position AFTER Ma1<>e1 (Black to move), resetSearchState(), search depth 1. Also search the position AFTER Re8xe1 (White to move, already stalemate) at depth 1; that one must score 0.

If the Black-to-move search's best move is Re8xe1 and the score is not 0, the horizon stalemate is mis-scored. Fix src/ai/search.ts so a position with no legal moves and not in check scores 0 even when it is reached at depth 0. Do not treat "no captures" as stalemate; quiet moves may remain. Re-read search.ts before editing. Keep the insufficientMaterial check and the no-king mate check.

If Black has a better move than the stalemate and the already-stalemate position scores 0, do not change search. Lock the scores you measured.

Run: npx vitest run src/ai/stalemate-horizon.test.ts src/ai/maester-safe-escape.test.ts src/ai/king-draw.test.ts

Return: both scores, whether search.ts changed, and the best move from the post-swap position.
last_assistant_text:
**Scores:** post-swap (Black) depth 1 → **1666**; after Re8xe1 (stalemate) depth 1 → **0**

**`search.ts` changed:** yes — no legal moves and not in check returns 0 before quiesce, including at depth 0

**Best move from post-swap:** `Re8-a8`

Before the fix, depth 1 preferred `Re8xe1` at +1689 (horizon stalemate scored as material). After the fix, Black prefers the quiet rook move; `maester-safe-escape`’s locked depth-2 score is now −1666. All three requested tests pass.
